disclaimer: Fixed, labelled benchmark measured offline. Not computed from your scan and not updated by it.
source: README.md, section 'Evaluation (malicious-package detection)'; measured with scripts/evaluate_dataset.py (rules as of commit ca4628c, 2026-11-01)
task: Is this npm package malicious? 'Flagged' = a malicious-behaviour finding with severity medium or higher.
malware_source: DataDog malicious-software-packages-dataset (Apache-2.0), commit 3fc8a1f; samples read in memory from encrypted zips, never extracted, installed or run

detectors.rules: TRACII's own static behaviour rules (backend/tracii/detect/static_rules.py), as text, without running code. The number that matters for new, unreported malware.
detectors.rules_plus_osv: Rules plus the OSV known-malware list (MAL- records). OSV only knows already-reported malware, and every sample here was reported, which flatters it.

sets.name: Fresh unseen set 2 (current rules)
notes: 0/40 false alarms on popular packages, 0/20 on older (2023-24) releases of popular packages, 0/18 on packages with install scripts
Rules catch 66% of the malware samples that contain code; some samples are a bare package.json and count as misses

caveats: Each set was locked before that round of rule changes and run once; these holdouts are now used up.
Small samples: read the 95% intervals, not the decimals.
Labels are DataDog's and were not independently verified. Benign packages skew newer than the malware. Packages over 25 MB were skipped.
GuardDog was not run on the malware (it needs an on-disk copy).
Raw per-sample outputs are not committed (results/*.local.json are git-ignored); reproduce with the commands in the README.
